title: Cinnamon rolls
summary: Soft spirals of psyllium-bound almond dough rolled around butter, cinnamon and sweetener, finished with a cream-cheese glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F) and grease a 20 cm (8 in) round cake pan.

For the dough, whisk the almond flour, coconut flour, psyllium, baking powder, salt and erythritol. Add the eggs, melted butter and warm water and mix to a soft dough. Let it rest 10 minutes; the psyllium firms it so it can be rolled.
Roll the dough between two sheets of parchment into a rectangle about 25 × 35 cm (10 × 14 in).
Spread with the softened butter and sprinkle with the allulose, cinnamon and cardamom.
Using the parchment to help, roll up from a long side into a firm log. Chill 5 minutes, then cut into 8 slices with a sharp knife and set them cut side up in the pan.
Bake 22–25 minutes, until golden. Allulose browns quickly, so cover loosely with foil if the tops darken before 20 minutes.
Beat the glaze ingredients until smooth and spread over the warm rolls.
dairy_free_notes: Dairy-free butter and cream cheese work well; the glaze is a little thinner, so add the almond milk a few drops at a time.
tips: The dough cracks if rolled too thin — about 6 mm (¼ in) is right.
There is no yeast: grain-free dough has no gluten to trap gas, so baking powder does the lifting.

origin.history: The Swedish kanelbulle, a cardamom-scented yeast bun rolled with cinnamon and butter, became a staple of Swedish coffee breaks in the decades after the First World War, as butter and sugar became more affordable. Sweden marks a Cinnamon Bun Day each 4 October. The American cinnamon roll belongs to the same northern European family.
